title: Run kinetic Monte Carlo simulations and record center deviation
action: Implement the 3D lattice kinetic Monte Carlo model for particle deposition on a template-patterned surface (lattice 100a×100a×2a, Au square templates width 14a, height 4a or varied, period 50a, periodic boundary conditions). Use the pair interaction, diffusion barrier, and Arrhenius hop rate as described in the instruction. For each of the required parameter combinations (varying ε_pp from 0.9 to 2.3 with ε_ps=0.3, ε_pg=1.3; varying ε_ps from 0.2 to 1.0 with ε_pp=1.6, ε_pg=1.3; and varying square height 0, 2a, 4a with ε_pp=2.3, ε_ps=0.3, ε_pg=1.3), run the simulation for up to 10,000 deposited particles (deposit one particle per 10,000 MC steps). At regular intervals (e.g., every 100 deposited particles) record the center deviation r (Euclidean distance between the center of mass of the deposited organic particles and the template square center). Output a single CSV file containing all results.
description: CSV file containing the center deviation r as a function of the number of deposited particles for all specified parameter sets. This raw data is the basis for the checker to evaluate whether the trends match the expected mechanisms.
output_schema: CSV with header: condition_label, particle_count, r. condition_label is a string uniquely identifying the parameter set (e.g., 'epp_0.9_eps_0.3_height_4'). particle_count is a non-negative integer. r is a float representing the center deviation in units of the lattice constant a.
